title: Arkansas Conversation Strategy
subtitle: Eyeball-to-Eyeball Organizing Doctrine
corePrinciple: People do not change their minds because of ads. People change their minds because of trusted relationships. The campaign wins through conversations.
notThis: Not a campaign tactic. A campaign doctrine.

visibilityVsVotes.doctrine: You need both — but the vote engine is relationships, not attendance counts.

successQuestion: How many new relationship leaders emerged?

conversationLadder.name: Meet & Greet
conversationLadder.description: Small group introduction to Kelly or surrogate

conversationLadder.name: Surrogate
conversationLadder.description: Carries Kelly's message into rooms she cannot reach this week

powerOf5Engine.firstAsk: Will you help us find five people?
powerOf5Engine.secondAsk: Will those five help us find five more?

trustNotArgument: The campaign is not attempting to win arguments. The campaign is attempting to build trust.

crossPartyTrust.message: You do not have to agree with Kelly to work with Kelly.
crossPartyTrust.sosFrame: The Secretary of State serves every voter.
crossPartyTrust.goal: Build enough trust that Republican local leaders open their networks and introduce the campaign to other community leaders.

directDemocracyPlank.doctrine: The people of Arkansas should have a meaningful pathway to propose laws, repeal laws, and place issues before voters.
directDemocracyPlank.sosRole: The Secretary of State's office should help citizens understand and navigate the process, regardless of whether the office agrees with the issue being proposed.

stopCommandCenterPrompt: After every stop: How many people moved up the conversation ladder? How many new relationship leaders emerged?
